claim: SHIP2 contains a construct spanning residues 420–878 corresponding to the Ptase and a C2 domain (Ptase-C2).
source: A construct of human SHIP2 containing residues 420–878 corresponding to the Ptase and a C2 domain (Ptase-C2) was crystallized and diffraction data collected to 1.96 Å.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the construct boundaries and domain composition.

claim: SHIP2 Ptase-C2 crystallized in the P212121 space group with eight molecules per asymmetric unit.
source: The protein crystallized in the P212121 space group with eight molecules per asymmetric unit (for crystallographic and refinement statistics, see Table 1).
evidence: Crystallographic data are provided in the text and Table 1.

claim: Each of the eight molecules in the asymmetric unit contains a 5-Ptase and a C2 domain.
source: Each of the eight molecules (A-H) contains a 5-Ptase and a C2 domain (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text states this and refers to Figure 1B showing the structure.

claim: The overall structure of the Ptase domain in Ptase-C2 is similar to previously reported structures.
source: The overall structure of the Ptase domain in Ptase-C2 is similar to the one previously reported (Mills et al., 2012; Trésaugues et al., 2014), displaying a central β-sheet sandwich decorated by seven helices (α1-α7) and several loops (L1-L4) (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text compares the structure to previous reports and cites them.

claim: Loop residues 587–594 (L3) are located at the interface with the C2 domain and are well ordered due to extensive interactions with the C2 domain.
source: Loop residues 587–594 (L3) are located at the interface with the C2 domain and are due to extensive interactions with the C2 domain well ordered (Figure 1C).
evidence: The text describes the structural observation and refers to Figure 1C.

claim: Loop L4 (residues 674–684) was disordered or closed over the active site in previous Ptase structures.
source: Importantly, a loop proximal to the active site, spanning residues 674–684 (L4), was in previous Ptase structures disordered or closed over the active site (Mills et al., 2012; Trésaugues et al., 2014) (Figure 1D; hereafter referred to as L4-in conformation)
evidence: The text describes previous structural observations with citations.

claim: Six of the Ptase-C2 monomers (A, B, C, E, F, G) exhibit a conformation where L4 points away from the active site (L4-out).
source: whereas in our structure 6 of the Ptase-C2 monomers (A, B, C, E, F, G) exhibit a conformation where L4 points away from the active site (L4-out).
evidence: The text explicitly states the number and identity of monomers with L4-out conformation.

claim: L4-out conformations are stabilized by interactions of R682 in L4 with one or two aspartic acids (D613/D615) adjacent to helix α5.
source: These L4-out conformations are stabilized by interactions of R682 in L4 with one or two aspartic acids (D613/D615) adjacent to helix α5 (Figure 1E–F, hereafter referred to as singly or doubly bound L4-out conformations).
evidence: The text describes the stabilizing interactions and refers to figures.

claim: The displacement of the guanidinium group of the R682 side chain is approximately 20 Å between L4-in and L4-out conformations.
source: Together, these conformations suggest extensive mobility of L4 with a displacement of the guanidinium group of the R682 side chain by ~20 Å between L4-in and L4-out conformations.
evidence: The text provides a quantitative measurement of the displacement.

claim: L4-out conformations appear to be favored by the presence of the C2 domain.
source: L4-out conformations appear to be favored by the presence of the C2 domain, since they are only observed for Ptase-C2, although crystal packing analysis suggests ample space in Ptase crystals in this region.
evidence: The text states this observation based on comparison of structures.

claim: In L4-out structures where R682 is doubly bound to D613 and D615, a network of hydrogen bonds is established that includes H674, T683 and N684 on L4, rigidifying the loop.
source: In L4-out structures where R682 is doubly bound to D613 and D615 (molecules B and F), a network of hydrogen bonds is established that includes H674, T683 and N684 on L4, rigidifying the loop (Figure 1F).
evidence: The text describes the hydrogen bond network observed in the structure.

claim: The C2 domain interacts with the Ptase on a face that is opposite to the active site.
source: The C2 domain interacts with the Ptase on a face that is opposite to the active site (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text describes the location of the interaction and refers to a figure.

claim: The Ptase and C2 domains share an extensive interface of 940 Å2.
source: The Ptase and C2 domains share an extensive interface of 940 Å2 (Figure 1C), resulting in stabilization of the Ptase (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The text provides a quantitative measurement of the interface area.

claim: The interface between Ptase and C2 domains results in stabilization of the Ptase.
source: The Ptase and C2 domains share an extensive interface of 940 Å2 (Figure 1C), resulting in stabilization of the Ptase (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The text states this and refers to supplementary data.

claim: The interface is constituted largely of hydrophobic interactions, with A592, F593, L597, Y697 and P698 in the Ptase and Y770, H820, L822, E836, V838 and A840 in the C2 domain forming a hydrophobic core.
source: The interface is constituted largely of hydrophobic interactions, with A592, F593, L597, Y697 and P698 in the Ptase and Y770, H820, L822, E836, V838 and A840 in the C2 domain forming a hydrophobic core (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text lists specific residues involved in hydrophobic interactions.

claim: A significant peripheral polar contact is formed by R649 in the Ptase, forming hydrogen bonds with E862 and a cation-π interaction with F855 in the C2 domain.
source: A significant peripheral polar contact is formed by R649 in the Ptase, forming hydrogen bonds with E862 and a cation-π interaction with F855 in the C2 domain.
evidence: The text describes specific polar interactions observed in the structure.

claim: R649 is located in a loop that connects to a stretch of three helices (α5–7), which at the other end join to D613 and D615, the docking site for R682 in the L4-out conformation.
source: Notably, R649 is located in a loop that connects to a stretch of three helices (α5–7, colored grey in Figure 1), which at the other end join to D613 and D615, the docking site for R682 in the L4-out conformation.
evidence: The text describes the structural connectivity.

claim: The structure confirms the presence of a β-sheet sandwich structure typical of C2 domains within residues 746–874 of SHIP2.
source: Our structure confirms the presence of a β-sheet sandwich structure typical of C2 domains within residues 746–874 of SHIP2.
evidence: The text explicitly states this structural confirmation.

claim: The closest structural homologues to the SHIP2 C2 domain are the C2 domains of the itchy E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (pdb code 2NQ3, Z score = 12.7, RMSD over 106 residues = 2.1 Å) and dysferlin (pdb code 4IQH, Z score = 12.4, RMSD over 110 residues = 2.4 Å).
source: Using the DaliLite server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010), we identified the closest structural homologues as the C2 domains of the itchy E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (pdb code 2NQ3, Z score = 12.7, RMSD over 106 residues = 2.1 Å) and dysferlin (pdb code 4IQH, Z score = 12.4, RMSD over 110 residues = 2.4 Å), which both belong to the PKC type C2 subfamily (Zhang and Aravind, 2010).
evidence: The text reports results from structural comparison using DaliLite.

claim: The itchy and dysferlin C2 domains both belong to the PKC type C2 subfamily.
source: Using the DaliLite server (Holm and Rosenström, 2010), we identified the closest structural homologues as the C2 domains of the itchy E3 ubiquitin protein ligase (pdb code 2NQ3, Z score = 12.7, RMSD over 106 residues = 2.1 Å) and dysferlin (pdb code 4IQH, Z score = 12.4, RMSD over 110 residues = 2.4 Å), which both belong to the PKC type C2 subfamily (Zhang and Aravind, 2010).
evidence: The text states this classification with a citation.

claim: A sequence-based similarity search using HH-pred identified the C2 domain of dysferlin as the closest related C2 domain (E-value = 0.049), although with 16% sequence identity the homology is low.
source: A sequence-based similarity search using HH-pred (Söding et al., 2005) also identified the C2 domain of dysferlin as the closest related C2 domain (E-value = 0.049), although with 16% sequence identity the homology is low.
evidence: The text reports results from sequence similarity search.

claim: The topology adopted by the SHIP2 C2 domain is that of type II (or P-variant).
source: The topology adopted by the SHIP2 C2 domain is as for itchy and dysferlin that of type II (or P-variant) (Corbalan-Garcia and Gómez-Fernández, 2014).
evidence: The text states the topology type with a citation.

claim: PKC type C2 domains usually bind phospholipids, most frequently phosphatidylserine (PS), often in a Ca2+-dependent manner via acidic residues present in three Ca2+-binding loops (CBLs) at the tip of the C2 domain.
source: PKC type C2 domains usually bind phospholipids, most frequently phosphatidylserine (PS), often in a Ca2+-dependent manner via acidic residues present in three Ca2+-binding loops (CBLs) at the tip of the C2 domain (Figure 2A–B) (Cho and Stahelin, 2006).
evidence: The text describes general properties of PKC type C2 domains with a citation.

claim: Only 2 of 5 acidic residues on CBL1 and CBL3 are conserved between PKCα and SHIP2 (D829 and E832) and two are replaced by serines (S761 and S827).
source: Structure-based sequence alignment indicates that only 2 of 5 acidic residues on CBL1 and CBL3 are conserved between PKCα and SHIP2 (D829 and E832) and two are replaced by serines (S761 and S827).
evidence: The text reports results from sequence alignment analysis.

claim: Both the Ptase and Ptase-C2 bind PS, with the C2 domain enhancing the interaction.
source: We found that both the Ptase and Ptase-C2 bind PS, with the C2 domain enhancing the interaction (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text reports experimental results from SPR and PLO assays.

claim: PS binding of Ptase-C2 exhibits a small increase of approximately 10% in presence of Ca2+.
source: SPR experiments reveal that PS binding of Ptase-C2 exhibits a small increase of ~10% in presence of Ca2+ (Figure 2D), an effect that was not detected in PLO experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from SPR experiments.

claim: The small effect of Ca2+ suggests that the PS interaction is dominated by direct PS binding to basic residues, rather than Ca2+-mediated binding to acidic residues and serines.
source: In summary, we conclude that both, the Ptase and Ptase-C2 bind PS and the small effect of Ca2+suggests that the interaction is dominated by direct PS binding to basic residues, rather than Ca2+-mediated binding to acidic residues and serines.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of the experimental results.

claim: The low conservation of Ca2+-binding residues in CBL1 and CBL3 of the SHIP2 C2 domain might weakly contribute to Ca2+-mediated lipid binding.
source: Nevertheless, the low conservation of Ca2+-binding residues in CBL1 and CBL3 of the SHIP2 C2 domain might weakly contribute to Ca2+-mediated lipid binding (Figure 2D).
evidence: The text provides a speculative interpretation.

claim: The C2 domain increases turnover rates for both IP4 and PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8 substrates.
source: We find that the C2 domain increases turnover rates for both substrates (Figure 3A–B, Table 2).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics experiments.

claim: The effect of the C2 domain is significantly larger with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, where the C2 domain increases the kcat approximately 10 fold, while for IP4 the increase is approximately 1.5 fold.
source: Interestingly, the effect is significantly larger with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, where the C2 domain increases the kcat ~10 fold, while for IP4 the increase is ~1.5 fold.
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The C2 domain switches the substrate preference with the Ptase alone turning over IP4 twice as fast as PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, whereas Ptase-C2 displays approximately 4 fold faster kinetics with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8 compared to IP4.
source: As a result, the C2 domain switches the substrate preference with the Ptase alone turning over IP4 twice as fast as PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, whereas Ptase-C2 displays ~ 4 fold faster kinetics with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8 compared to IP4 (Table 2).
evidence: The text reports quantitative comparison of kinetic parameters.

claim: The KM is less affected by the C2 domain with a significant change only with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, where the absence of the C2 domain decreases the KM approximately 2 fold.
source: The KM is less affected by the C2 domain with a significant change only with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, where the absence of the C2 domain decreases the KM ~ 2 fold (Table 2).
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The fact that the distant C2 domain has specific and differential effects on catalysis of the two substrates suggests the presence of an allosteric communication between the domain interface and the active site.
source: The fact that the distant C2 domain has specific and differential effects on catalysis of the two substrates, suggests the presence of an allosteric communication between the domain interface and the active site (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of the kinetic data.

claim: The FLDD mutations largely mimic the absence of the C2 domain in terms of catalytic turnover.
source: When comparing the catalytic turnover of the FLDD mutants we find that the C2 domain no longer has a significant effect with either substrate (Figure 3C–D, Table 2), indicating that the FLDD mutations largely mimic the absence of the C2 domain.
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with mutants.

claim: The FLDD mutations increase intrinsic Ptase activity with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8.
source: We note that the FLDD mutations increase intrinsic Ptase activity with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8, but importantly the presence of the C2 does not cause any further change.
evidence: The text reports an observation from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The polar R649A mutation specifically eliminates the effect of the C2 domain on IP4 kinetics, while retaining most of its effect on PI(3,4,5)P3.
source: Interestingly, the polar R649A mutation specifically eliminates the effect of the C2 domain on IP4 kinetics, while retaining most of its effect on PI(3,4,5)P3 (Figure 3E–F).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with the R649A mutant.

claim: The polar R649-E682/F855 interactions between Ptase and C2 domains mainly affect SHIP2 activity with IP4, whereas hydrophobic interactions increase activity towards PI(3,4,5)P3.
source: Together, these results suggest that the polar R649-E682/F855 interactions between Ptase and C2 domains mainly affect SHIP2 activity with IP4, whereas hydrophobic interactions increase activity towards PI(3,4,5)P3.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of the mutagenesis results.

claim: Soluble PS-diC8 has little effect on IP4 kinetics and increases activity approximately 40% with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8.
source: We find that soluble PS-diC8 has little effect on IP4 kinetics and increases activity ~40% with PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8 (Figure 4A–B), both for Ptase and Ptase-C2.
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from enzyme kinetics.

claim: The presence of 30% (mol/mol) PS-diC16 in vesicles increases SHIP2 activity approximately 2–3 fold for both Ptase and Ptase-C2 with lipid vesicle embedded PI(3,4,5)P3-diC16 substrate.
source: If instead a lipid vesicle embedded PI(3,4,5)P3-diC16 substrate is used, the presence of 30% (mol/mol) PS-diC16 in the vesicles increases SHIP2 activity ~2–3 fold for both, Ptase and Ptase-C2 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from enzyme kinetics with vesicles.

claim: The PS-mediated increase in activity on vesicles is maintained for the FLDD mutant.
source: The PS-mediated increase in activity on vesicles is maintained for the FLDD mutant, whereas as with soluble substrates, the increase in activity due to the C2 domain is abrogated by the interface mutations (Figure 4D).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with the FLDD mutant on vesicles.

claim: The effect of PS is amplified for SHIP activity on vesicles, possibly due to a localization or positioning effect and this effect is independent and additive to the enhancing allosteric signaling of the C2 domain.
source: In summary, these data show that the effect of PS is amplified for SHIP activity on vesicles, possibly due to a localization or positioning effect and this effect is independent and additive to the enhancing allosteric signaling of the C2 domain.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of the PS effects on enzyme activity.

claim: The C2 domain induces several dynamic changes in the Ptase domain, as can be seen from root mean square fluctuations (RMSF) throughout the simulation.
source: The simulations indicate that the C2 domain induces several dynamic changes in the Ptase domain, as can be seen from root mean square fluctuations (RMSF) throughout the simulation (Figure 5A).
evidence: The text reports results from MD simulations.

claim: L3 is strongly stabilized due to its direct interaction with the C2 domain.
source: Not surprisingly, L3 is strongly stabilized due to its direct interaction with the C2 domain.
evidence: The text reports an observation from MD simulations.

claim: L2 (residues 531–539) and L4 fluctuate stronger in presence of the C2 domain.
source: On the other hand, L2 (residues 531–539) and L4 fluctuate stronger in presence of the C2 domain.
evidence: The text reports results from MD simulations.

claim: Higher L4 fluctuations occur when L4 is detached from D613/D615.
source: RMSF analysis separated into different L4 states (R682 unbound, singly or doubly bound) indicate that higher L4 fluctuations occur when L4 is detached from D613/D615 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text reports results from MD simulation analysis.

claim: Principal component analysis shows as one of the principal motions α5 moving away from α6.
source: Principal component analysis shows as one of the principal motions α5 moving away from α6 (Figure 5A insert, Videos 1–2).
evidence: The text reports results from PCA of MD simulations.

claim: In the presence of the C2 domain, the region of α5, α6 and the proximal D613/D615 remain closer to the R682 doubly bound starting structure, whereas in absence of the C2 domain this region deviates significantly from the starting conformation.
source: We find a significant difference in the region of α5, α6 and the proximal D613/D615, which in the presence of the C2 domain remain closer to the R682 doubly bound starting structure, whereas in absence of the C2 domain this region deviates significantly from the starting conformation (Figure 5B, also observed in Videos 1–2).
evidence: The text reports results from RMSD analysis of MD simulations.

claim: The deviation of α5, α6 and D613/D615 from the starting conformation occurs specifically in conformations where R682 is singly bound to either D613 or D615.
source: The same RMSD analysis of different L4 states indicates that this occurs specifically in conformations where R682 is singly bound to either D613 or D615 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The text reports results from RMSD analysis of MD simulations.

claim: Different α5 helix positions are observed in the Ptase-C2 crystal structure, confirming its mobility.
source: Interestingly, different α5 helix positions are also observed in the Ptase-C2 crystal structure, confirming its mobility, and in agreement with MD simulations helix α5 is shifted specifically in singly bound R682 conformations by ~1.5 Å (Figure 5C).
evidence: The text reports observations from crystal structures and MD simulations.

claim: Helix α5 is shifted specifically in singly bound R682 conformations by approximately 1.5 Å.
source: Interestingly, different α5 helix positions are also observed in the Ptase-C2 crystal structure, confirming its mobility, and in agreement with MD simulations helix α5 is shifted specifically in singly bound R682 conformations by ~1.5 Å (Figure 5C).
evidence: The text reports a quantitative measurement from structural analysis.

claim: The C2 induced increase of L4 fluctuations when L4 is unbound together with stabilized D613/D615 when R682 is singly docked could potentially favor the transition from L4-in to L4-out.
source: The C2 induced increase of L4 fluctuations when L4 is unbound (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A) together with stabilized D613/D615 when R682 is singly docked (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E) could potentially favor the transition from L4-in to L4-out and might be a reason why the L4-out conformation is only observed in Ptase-C2 crystal structures, but not in Ptase-only or Ptase-C2 FLDD structures.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of MD simulation and structural data.

claim: Once R682 detaches from D613/D615, a more sustained release of L4 is observed in MD simulations where the C2 domain is present.
source: On the other hand, once R682 detaches from D613/D615 we observe a more sustained release of L4 in MD simulations where the C2 domain is present.
evidence: The text reports results from MD simulations.

claim: In absence of the C2 domain R682 experiences only brief releases followed by immediate rebinding, whereas in the Ptase-C2 simulation R682 remains fully detached from D613/D615 for approximately 1 μs of the 4.35 μs simulation.
source: While in absence of the C2 domain R682 experiences only brief releases followed by immediate rebinding, in the Ptase-C2 simulation R682 remains fully detached from D613/D615 for ~1 μs of the 4.35 μs simulation (Figure 5D).
evidence: The text reports quantitative results from MD simulations.

claim: For the Ptase alone all of the main clusters remain in a L4-out conformation, whereas for Ptase-C2 the third most populated cluster has R682 detached from D613/D615.
source: Indeed, cluster analysis of snapshots from the simulation reveals that for the Ptase alone all of the main clusters remain in a L4-out conformation, whereas for Ptase-C2 the third most populated cluster has R682 detached from D613/D615 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G–H).
evidence: The text reports results from cluster analysis of MD simulations.

claim: The data support a communication between the C2 domain and the active site in the Ptase by modulating the dynamics of helices α5–7 and L4 to facilitate transitions between L4-in and L4-out conformations.
source: Together, these data support a communication between the C2 domain and the active site in the Ptase by modulating the dynamics of helices α5–7 and L4 to facilitate transitions between L4-in and L4-out conformations.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of MD simulation results.

claim: A communication via R649 is suggested, since this residue connects helices α5–7 to the C2 domain.
source: Structurally, this suggests a communication via R649, since this residue connects helices α5–7 to the C2 domain.
evidence: The text provides a structural interpretation.

claim: A key 4 P interacting residue is N684 on L4.
source: In this complex the catalytic base D607 stabilizes a water molecule for 5 P attack. According to our model a key 4 P interacting residue is N684 on L4.
evidence: The text describes a model based on structural data.

claim: N684 can adopt two conformations and needs to point towards the active site to interact with the substrate 4 P, which is seen in unbound or singly bound, but not doubly bound L4 conformations.
source: N684 can adopt two conformations (Figures 1D–F and 5C) and needs to point towards the active site to interact with the substrate 4 P, which is seen in unbound or singly bound, but not doubly bound L4 conformations.
evidence: The text describes observations from crystal structures.

claim: In the L4-in conformation, R682 is ideally positioned to interact with the 3 P of PI(3,4,5)P3.
source: In our model L4 adopts the L4-in conformation seen in 2 SHIP2 Ptase structures (PDB: 3NR8 and 4A9C; Mills et al., 2012; Trésaugues et al., 2014). In this conformation R682 is ideally positioned to interact with the 3 P of PI(3,4,5)P3.
evidence: The text describes a model based on structural data.

claim: The C2 domain significantly restricts the displacement of the headgroup of both IP4 and PI(3,4,5)P3-diC8 substrates away from the Michaelis-Menten complex.
source: Interestingly, the C2 domain significantly restricts the displacement of the headgroup of both substrates away from the Michaelis-Menten complex (Figure 6C–D, Videos 3–4).
evidence: The text reports results from MD simulations with substrate bound.

claim: Co-crystallization experiments using the catalytically inactive SHIP Ptase-C2 D607A mutant with Mg2+ and substrate failed to reveal clear electron density for the substrate.
source: Co-crystallization experiments using the catalytically inactive SHIP Ptase-C2 D607A mutant with Mg2+ and substrate failed to reveal clear electron density for the substrate.
evidence: The text reports results from crystallization experiments.

claim: The co-crystallization experiments with D607A exhibited electron density corresponding to a Mg2+ ion and a phosphate group.
source: Although our co-crystallization experiments did not reveal bound substrate they did exhibit electron density corresponding to a Mg2+ ion and a phosphate group (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text reports observations from crystal structures.

claim: The Mg2+ ion is on average displaced by 1.3 Å and the phosphate by 1.7 Å compared to the Mg2+ and 5 P positions in the model.
source: The Mg2+ ion is on average displaced by 1.3 Å and the phosphate by 1.7 Å compared to the Mg2+ and 5 P positions in our model (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text reports quantitative measurements from structural analysis.

claim: The position of the phosphate does not leave space for an attacking water bound to D607, hence this could represent the post-catalysis positions of the Mg2+ and 5 P.
source: The position of the phosphate does not leave space for an attacking water bound to D607, hence this could represent the post-catalysis positions of the Mg2+ and 5 P.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of structural data.

claim: D613A/D615A mutated Ptase-C2 behaves similar to the R649A mutant, in that both only affect turnover with IP4, but have little effect on PI(3,4,5)P3 kinetics.
source: Interestingly, D613A/D615A mutated Ptase-C2 behaves similar to the R649A mutant, in that both only affect turnover with IP4, but have little effect on PI(3,4,5)P3 kinetics (Figures 3E–F and 7B–C).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with mutants.

claim: The similitude in behavior between D613A/D615A and R649A mutants supports an allosteric communication via R649 and D613/D615.
source: This similitude in behavior supports an allosteric communication via R649 and D613/D615.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of mutagenesis results.

claim: The R682A and N684A mutants have lost most of their activity.
source: Further, we find that the R682A and N684A mutants have lost most of their activity (Table 3; note that for N684A this is also the case for the CD-stable Ptase-C2 form), supporting a key role for these residues in substrate binding via 3 P and 4 P, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with mutants.

claim: R682 and N684 have a key role in substrate binding via 3 P and 4 P, respectively.
source: Further, we find that the R682A and N684A mutants have lost most of their activity (Table 3; note that for N684A this is also the case for the CD-stable Ptase-C2 form), supporting a key role for these residues in substrate binding via 3 P and 4 P, respectively (Figure 6A).
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of mutagenesis results.

claim: R691 links the Ptase core β-sandwich with helices α5–7.
source: R691 links the Ptase core β-sandwich with helices α5–7 (Figure 7A) and its mutation inactivates Ptase-C2, which together with the changed CD spectra indicates a structural role for this residue.
evidence: The text describes structural observations.

claim: Mutation of R691 inactivates Ptase-C2, which together with the changed CD spectra indicates a structural role for this residue.
source: R691 links the Ptase core β-sandwich with helices α5–7 (Figure 7A) and its mutation inactivates Ptase-C2, which together with the changed CD spectra indicates a structural role for this residue.
evidence: The text reports results from mutagenesis and CD spectroscopy.

claim: R665A mainly affects the Ptase domain, but has little effect on Ptase-C2 activity.
source: Unexpectedly, R665A mainly affects the Ptase domain, but has little effect on Ptase-C2 activity (Figure 7D–E, Table 3).
evidence: The text reports results from enzyme kinetics with the R665A mutant.

claim: According to the model, R665 stabilizes a water molecule in the coordination sphere of the Mg2+ ion.
source: According to our model, R665 stabilizes a water molecule in the coordination sphere of the Mg2+ ion (Figure 6B).
evidence: The text describes a model based on structural data.

claim: MD simulations show C2-mediated stabilization of the substrate headgroup, apparently making the R665-mediated stabilization dispensable in presence of the C2 domain.
source: This fits with MD simulations showing C2-mediated stabilization of the substrate headgroup (Figure 6C–D), apparently making the R665-mediated stabilization dispensable in presence of the C2 domain.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of MD simulation and mutagenesis results.

claim: The results support an allosteric communication from the C2 domain via R649 and helices α5–7 to L4, which by changing their dynamic behavior affects enzyme kinetics with the IP4 headgroup.
source: Together, these results support an allosteric communication from the C2 domain via R649 and helices α5–7 to L4, which by changing their dynamic behavior affects enzyme kinetics with the IP4 headgroup.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of mutagenesis and MD simulation results.

claim: The results support an overall stabilization of the Ptase active site by the C2 domain allowing both substrates to bind in a catalytically productive mode.
source: In addition, they support an overall stabilization of the Ptase active site by the C2 domain allowing both substrates to bind in a catalytically productive mode.
evidence: The text provides an interpretation of mutagenesis and MD simulation results.

claim: Expressing wild-type SHIP2 causes a significant reduction in downstream Akt phosphorylation levels.
source: Expressing wild-type SHIP2 causes a significant reduction in downstream Akt phosphorylation levels (Figure 8).
evidence: The text reports results from cell-based assays.

claim: Removing the C2 domain abolishes observed SHIP2 activity in cells.
source: Removing the C2 domain abolishes observed SHIP2 activity, whereas the FLDD mutations partially reduce activity of the wild-type protein.
evidence: The text reports results from cell-based assays.

claim: The FLDD mutations partially reduce activity of the wild-type SHIP2 protein in cells.
source: Removing the C2 domain abolishes observed SHIP2 activity, whereas the FLDD mutations partially reduce activity of the wild-type protein.
evidence: The text reports results from cell-based assays.

claim: C2 interactions observed in the crystal structure are important for SHIP2 activity in cells.
source: This confirms that C2 interactions observed in the crystal structure are important for SHIP2 activity in cells.
